Multiple values must be selectable — use Combobox with multiple (selections render as chips).

disambiguateFrom.distinction: Select is the custom Radix listbox with popper positioning and rich item rendering; NativeSelect wraps the browser's <select> for platform-native pickers. Pick NativeSelect for simple/mobile forms, Select for design-system-styled menus.
RadioGroup exposes all choices inline for a small set; NativeSelect collapses choices behind a control. Use RadioGroup under 4 options, NativeSelect for 4+.
A Combobox adds type-to-filter over a large list and supports multi-select chips; NativeSelect has no typeahead beyond the browser default. Reach for Combobox when filtering matters.
Menu triggers actions/commands; NativeSelect picks a form value. Use NativeSelect when the result is a selected value, Menu for an action list.

items.name: app-icon
items.title: AppIcon
items.description: Typed component for 244 third-party service logos synced from Figma. Five sizes (20, 24, 28, 40, 48px) and three variants (color, mono, outline).

useWhen: Showing a recognizable third-party or first-party service logo (Spotify, Instagram, PayPal) by its app name.
Building link or platform lists where each row needs its brand mark at a fixed size (20/24/28/40/48px).
You need a monochrome (currentColor) or stroke outline treatment of a brand logo, not just full color.
You want a typed app prop with a graceful fallback when a logo key is missing.
notWhen: You need a generic UI glyph (chevron, search, trash) — import from @linktr.ee/arbor/icons (Phosphor) instead.
You need a clickable icon control — wrap it in IconButton instead.
The mark is a custom one-off not in the synced set — add an SVG to the Figma source or use a plain img.
You want to import it from the main barrel — AppIcon ships only via the @linktr.ee/arbor/components/AppIcon subpath to protect tree-shaking.

disambiguateFrom.distinction: icons re-exports the full Phosphor set of generic UI glyphs; AppIcon renders specific brand/service logos by name. Reach for icons for interface symbols, AppIcon for a recognizable product mark.

IconButton is an interactive button with an icon; AppIcon is a non-interactive presentational logo. Wrap AppIcon in IconButton (or a link) when it needs to be clickable, use AppIcon alone for display.
Avatar fits a person or entity portrait with initials fallback; AppIcon is a fixed brand mark. Use AppIcon for a logo, Avatar for user/profile imagery.

items.name: fieldset
items.title: Fieldset
items.description: Semantic grouping for form controls. Wraps radio, checkbox, and other primitives with a legend and description.

useWhen: Grouping related radio or checkbox controls under one visible question or legend.
You need native <fieldset>/<legend> semantics so screen readers announce the group label per option.
A set of controls shares one description or one validation error message.
Pairing with RadioGroup or grouped Checkboxes that have no built-in group label.
notWhen: Labeling a single input with its own label and message — use Field instead.
You want a two-column title-plus-input settings row — use Field.Root layout="horizontal" instead.
You need a plain visual container with no form semantics — use a bordered container or Card.
The control already provides its own group role, like Radix RadioGroup with an aria-label.

disambiguateFrom.distinction: Field wraps one input with label, message, and counter; Fieldset groups multiple controls under a shared legend. Pick Field for a single control, Fieldset for a related set.
RadioGroup already provides role=radiogroup; wrap it in Fieldset only to add a visible <legend>. For an invisible label, put aria-label on RadioGroup and skip Fieldset.

Card is a generic visual container with no form semantics; Fieldset is a semantic form grouping. Use Fieldset to group form controls for assistive tech, Card only for visual containment without group labeling.

items.name: one-time-password-field
items.title: One-Time Password Field
items.description: Segmented one-time-password (OTP) input built on input-otp. Per-slot boxes with auto-advance, paste distribution, a blinking caret, and one-time-code autofill. Composes with Field for label, error state, and message.

useWhen: Entering a short, fixed-length one-time code — an SMS or email verification code, a 2FA code, or a PIN to unlock a link.
The code should read as discrete cells with auto-advance, and benefit from OS / password-manager one-time-code autofill.
A pasted code should distribute itself across the cells automatically.
Wrapping in Field so a label, description, and error message describe the code input.
notWhen: Capturing free-form or variable-length text — use a Text Field (Field.Input); don't fake OTP entry with a maxLength text field.
Entering a password or long secret — use a password Field, not a segmented display that renders each character in its own cell.
The value is a single multi-character token where per-character segmentation adds no clarity.
Choosing among options — use Checkbox, RadioGroup, or Select.

disambiguateFrom.distinction: A Text Field is one continuous input for free-form, variable-length text; OneTimePasswordField is segmented, fixed-length, auto-advances per character, and distributes pasted codes. Use a Text Field for normal input, OneTimePasswordField only for short one-time codes.
A 'PIN input' is the same segmented one-time-code pattern — OneTimePasswordField is Arbor's implementation of it. There is no separate PIN component; set maxLength and render one Slot per digit.

items.name: sidebar
items.title: Sidebar
items.description: Persistent, collapsible app-shell navigation column with nested menus, icon-rail collapsing, tooltips, and an automatic off-canvas panel on mobile. Ships the Sheet panel it uses for that mobile branch — Sheet is Sidebar's internal implementation, not a component to reach for on its own.

useWhen: Building persistent, vertical app navigation that sits alongside content (e.g. an admin shell or settings layout).
Navigation benefits from collapsing to an icon rail without losing labels — collapsed labels surface as tooltips.
Grouping nested destinations (e.g. Payments and Payouts under Earn) under a parent item without inventing a second navigation surface.
notWhen: The panel is transient and triggered on demand for a one-off action list — use Menu instead.
You only need a top app bar with title and actions — use HeaderBar.
Navigation switches between peer views of the same content within one page or component — use Tabs.

disambiguateFrom.distinction: Menu is a transient, triggered list of actions or options that opens on demand and closes after a choice; Sidebar is always present (or, on mobile, present whenever the app shell is open) and represents where you are, not a one-off action list.

Tabs switches between views of the same content within a page or component; Sidebar switches between different top-level areas of the product, each with its own URL. Use Tabs for in-page sections, Sidebar for app-level nav.
HeaderBar is the horizontal top app bar (title plus actions); Sidebar is the vertical side rail. Pick by axis: top chrome → HeaderBar, side nav → Sidebar.

Drawer is a temporary, dismissible overlay panel; Sidebar is a persistent nav rail. Sidebar's own mobile off-canvas panel is built on Sheet, not Drawer — Drawer remains the pick for a genuinely temporary slide-in.
SideNav was the Figma-only working name for this spec before it shipped as Sidebar; treat SideNav references as the same shipped component, not a distinct one.

items.name: progress-bar
items.title: ProgressBar
items.description: Determinate linear progress indicator — a pill track with a fill whose width is the completion percentage. For measurable advancement toward a known end (upload, multi-step setup, quota). Not for indeterminate waits, where a Skeleton or spinner is the honest signal.

useWhen: Advancement toward a known end is measurable: bytes uploaded, steps completed, quota consumed.
The wait is long enough to be worth quantifying — past roughly 10 seconds, a percentage reassures where a placeholder does not.
A multi-step flow shows how much of the whole remains, not just that something is happening.
The surrounding layout already explains what is progressing, or you can name it with aria-label / aria-labelledby.
notWhen: Duration is unknown or unmeasurable — a determinate bar that sits at one value reads as broken. Use Skeleton for a structural load, or Button's loading state for a single action.
A page or content region whose layout is known is loading — Skeleton mimics the shape and communicates more.
One inline action is in flight, like a save or submit — use Button's state="loading".
The bar would render narrower than roughly 150px, where the fill is too small to read as progress.
You need a circular form or a value label inside the indicator — neither is built yet; see the scope note below.

disambiguateFrom.distinction: Skeleton is for indeterminate structural loads where the layout is known but the duration is not; ProgressBar communicates measurable advancement toward a known end. Pick ProgressBar past ~10 seconds or whenever progress is quantifiable.

A radial indicator for the same determinate job, used where space is tight or a circular form suits the layout. It is still in design (DS-691) and has no Arbor export — use ProgressBar until it ships rather than hand-rolling a ring.
A single inline action in flight is the button's own concern — reach for Button state="loading", not a bar next to it. ProgressBar is for a region or flow, not one control.

ProgressBar is determinate only — value is required. The approved design models no indeterminate, paused, or disabled state and specifies no motion for them, so they were deliberately not invented in code (DNG-1325). Use Skeleton for an unmeasurable wait.

items.name: arbor-tokens
items.title: Arbor Design Tokens
items.description: CSS custom properties for all Arbor design tokens including colors, spacing, shapes, typography, and theme variants. Import this CSS file at the root of your project.

items.name: arbor-tailwind-preset
items.title: Arbor Tailwind Preset
items.description: Complete Tailwind CSS preset with all Arbor design token mappings, custom utilities, and plugins. Add as a preset in your tailwind.config to enable all Arbor component styles.

items.name: setup
items.title: Arbor Setup
items.description: One-command setup for the Arbor design system. Installs design tokens (CSS variables), Tailwind preset, and the cn utility. Run: npx shadcn@latest add @arbor/setup
